rationale: The sheet does not yet read as a diverse 15-option portfolio; it reads as a small set of repeated chassis with minor roof or notch edits. The dominant language is box/bar-derived and carved-bar-derived, with many candidates differing only by tiny changes to front notches, lifts, or stepped roofs. That fails the portfolio test for visible family diversity and program-specific threshold language. The stronger candidates are the ones that actually register a usable void, threshold, or upper retreat, but even those are still too clustered. For the next run, the board needs clearer separation among courtyard, split, carve, terrace, and bent/cross relations so the mixed-use ground edge is legible and not just a repeated box family.

repeated_family_groups.shared_language: single oblique leaning-tower mass with a shallow top recess; reads as one-off object rather than a neighborhood threshold building
bar/block plus attached or clustered volume, same basic box-bar chassis with frontal notch or insert
stepped/terraced bar or monolith with only roofline variation; strong repeated bar footprint and similar upper stepping
carved or punctured monolith with a similar cuboid footprint and repeated void logic at the front edge
lifted or lifted-spine bar with small threshold cut; same section idea repeated with minor roof/void edits

required_next_relations: Develop one clearly public courtyard or split-wing family with a ground-level spine width in the contract range, so the void is occupied and usable rather than merely cut out.
Introduce one bent or crossed mass that makes the active ground edge read as an addressed street threshold, not just a roof or facade variation.
Create a terrace or setback family where the upper mass retreats to form a usable outdoor room, preserving calm upper massing above the active base.
Vary section depth: alternate lift, notch, carve, and split so the next board shows at least ten materially different spatial families instead of repeated box/bar chassis.
Avoid simple box-dominated and pyramidal readings; anchor the next run in threshold, void, and access relations tied to mixed-use ground program.
